Simple Present Tense vs. Simple past Tense
You use the simple present along with the simple past to contrast events and actions in different periods of time.

Sometimes we like to talk about how things are in the present and how different they were in the past. In order to express our ideas, it’s important to review the basic rules of these two tenses. 

Present Simple:

We use it to talk about routines and everyday actions. Remember that for the third person singular (He, She, It) you need to add “–s, -es, -ies” to the verbs in affirmative sentences.

Example:

Today, the Internet gives us a lot of tools to interact with others.

Past Simple:

We use it to talk about actions and events in the past. Remember that there are regular verbs (those that finish in –ed such as change - changed) and irregular verbs (those that change such as write-wrote).

Example:

Internet had a lot of restrictions.  

Present Simple vs. Past Simple

If we combine these two tenses, we can create a comparison between the present and the past.

Example:

Today, the internet connects millions of people around the world. In the past, only a few amount of people had access to it.
We need the Internet for many things nowadays, long time ago people didn't need it that much.
Nowadays, software programming evolves day by day thanks to the Internet age. In the past, a programmer who wanted to work on a software had to invest a lot of time and effort.
Its growth started in the mid-1990s, and it contributed to the development of programming languages by opening new platforms.
The Internet age also brought streamlining access which allows people to access to vast amounts of information.
Questions with Prepositions, "at" - "about"
We can usually use prepositions at the end of questions in any tense to be specific about the kind of information that we want to get.

About: Whenever we use the preposition about in a question, we demand information related to something’s content.

Structure:

Wh question + auxiliary + subject + verb + about? 

Example:

What did she talk about?

At: When we use at in questions, we usually want to know about the location of something.

Structure:

Wh question + auxiliary + subject + verb + at?

Example:

What are you looking at?
What are you staring at?
What are you concerned about?

The Importance of the Internet
The Internet has become a big part of our lives. Can you imagine how different things would be without the Internet?

The Internet has provided a lot of benefits to our world. It is capable of spreading all types of information across towns, cities, countries, and continents. The Internet has impacted education, healthcare, politics and every other field of science.

Let’s mention some benefits of the Internet:

  • People can access to different types of information.
  • People can socialize easier, regardless of the distance.
  • Science, culture, and entertainment are accessible to anyone.
  • Students are able to find many resources for their assignments.

It’s true that the internet may have some risks, sometimes the information you find there may not be correct, or there are people trying to use the Internet to harm others in various ways. The Internet is a wonderful thing, but everyone should be responsible when using it.

Cesar: Hey, Jessica. What are you staring at?
Jessica: Nothing. I'm just thinking.
Cesar: You seem a little distracted, what are you concerned about?
Jessica: Well, I run out of data on my phone, and I realized that most of the things I do during the day require me to be online.
Cesar: We are living in the Internet age. We need the Internet for many things nowadays, long time ago people didn't need it that much. In a near future, we won't know how to live without it.
Jessica: I know! The Internet has made a big impact in our lives.

Cesar: Its growth started in the mid-1990s, and it contributed to the development of programming languages by opening new platforms. The Internet age also brought streamlining access which allows people to access to vast amounts of information.
Jessica: What age are we in? Technology advances very fast. In the past, no one needed many technological devices as we need now.
Cesar: I will compare software programming to a library. After the Internet age, software programming has become one of the biggest trends in modern computing systems. Programmers need the Internet, not only as a source of general information but also as a big library of reusable codes.

Jessica: Interesting. However, software programmers are supposed to know how to develop software without an Internet connection, don't they? I understand that they can search for anything online, but is the Internet really necessary for everything?
Cesar: Nowadays, software programming evolves day by day thanks to the Internet age. In the past, a programmer who wanted to work on a software had to invest a lot of time and effort. Today, software programmers are able to communicate with their colleagues, so everyone gains experience from collaborating with other people around the world.
Jessica: Wow! You are an expert on this topic.
